CHAPTER 2.2 · LEARNING AREA 2

CHAPTER 2.2 · LEARNING AREA 2 · NOVEMBER · DECEMBER

Decimals and percentages

The receipt says €2.49, the folding ruler 1.35 m, the sprint 9.58 seconds, and the battery shows 75%. All of these are fractions in a different dress. You learn what the digits after the decimal point mean, how to convert fractions, decimals and percentages into one another and how to compare, order and round decimals.

8 LESSONS2 UNITS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • extend the place value table by tenths, hundredths and thousandths
  • write decimal fractions as decimals and the other way round
  • give important parts as percentages
  • compare, order and round decimals

UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Tenths, hundredths, thousandths

To the right of the ones come the tenths, then the hundredths, then the thousandths. Each place is again ten times smaller. So that you know where the ones stop, you put a decimal point: 3.47 means 3 ones, 4 tenths and 7 hundredths.

Fractions with the denominator 10, 100, 1000, … are called decimal fractions. They can be written straight away as a decimal. Other fractions are first expanded to a decimal fraction: $\tfrac34 = \tfrac{75}{100} = 0.75$.

KEY POINT · DECIMALS

$0.1 = \tfrac{1}{10}$ (one tenth) · $0.01 = \tfrac{1}{100}$ (one hundredth) · $0.001 = \tfrac{1}{1000}$ (one thousandth)

$3.47 = 3 + \tfrac{4}{10} + \tfrac{7}{100} = 3\tfrac{47}{100}$. You read “three point four seven”.

If you add zeros at the end, the value does not change: $0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500$. That is the same as expanding: $\tfrac{5}{10} = \tfrac{50}{100}$.

Do not read “forty-seven”: 3.47 is read “three point four seven”, not “three point forty-seven”. Otherwise 3.47 sounds bigger than 3.5.

Quantities: €2.49 is €2 and 49 cents · 1.35 m is 1 m and 35 cm · 0.5 kg is 500 g.

INTERACTIVE · THE PLACE VALUE TABLE WITH A DECIMAL POINT
EXAMPLE 1 · FRACTION TO DECIMAL

Write as a decimal: a) $\tfrac{7}{100}$   b) $\tfrac{3}{5}$   c) $2\tfrac{1}{8}$

a) $0.07$   b) $\tfrac35 = \tfrac{6}{10} = 0.6$   c) $\tfrac18 = \tfrac{125}{1000}$, so $2.125$

EXAMPLE 2 · DECIMAL TO FRACTION

Write as a fully simplified fraction: a) $0.4$   b) $0.25$   c) $1.04$

a) $\tfrac{4}{10} = \tfrac25$   b) $\tfrac{25}{100} = \tfrac14$   c) $1\tfrac{4}{100} = 1\tfrac{1}{25}$

EXERCISES

Write as a decimal: a) $\tfrac{9}{10}$   b) $\tfrac{23}{100}$   c) $\tfrac{5}{1000}$   d) $4\tfrac{3}{10}$   e) $\tfrac{108}{100}$

a) 0.9   b) 0.23   c) 0.005   d) 4.3   e) 1.08

What is the value of the digit 6 in a) 0.6   b) 2.06   c) 61.5   d) 4.006?

a) 6 tenths   b) 6 hundredths   c) 6 tens   d) 6 thousandths

Write with a decimal point in the unit given: a) 3 m 25 cm in m   b) €7 5 cents in €   c) 1 kg 250 g in kg   d) 45 cm in m

a) 3.25 m   b) €7.05   c) 1.25 kg   d) 0.45 m

First expand to a decimal fraction and then write as a decimal: a) $\tfrac{1}{4}$   b) $\tfrac{7}{20}$   c) $\tfrac{3}{8}$   d) $\tfrac{11}{25}$

a) $\tfrac{25}{100} = 0.25$   b) $\tfrac{35}{100} = 0.35$   c) $\tfrac{375}{1000} = 0.375$   d) $\tfrac{44}{100} = 0.44$

Why can $\tfrac{1}{3}$ not be expanded to a decimal fraction? What happens if you divide $1 \div 3$ on paper and keep going?

10, 100, 1000 have only the prime factors 2 and 5, so they are never divisible by 3. When dividing, the remainder is always 1: $0.333\dots$ The threes never stop. More on this in Year 6.

UNIT 24 LESSONS

2Per cent, comparing and rounding

“Per cent” comes from Latin and means “of a hundred”. 50% is 50 out of 100, i.e. half. 25% is a quarter, 100% is the whole. 10% of €200 is a tenth of it, i.e. €20.

KEY POINT · PER CENT

$1\% = \tfrac{1}{100} = 0.01$. Percentages are hundredths.

Fraction$\tfrac12$$\tfrac14$$\tfrac34$$\tfrac15$$\tfrac{1}{10}$$1$
Decimal0.50.250.750.20.11
Per cent50%25%75%20%10%100%
KEY POINT · COMPARING AND ROUNDING

Comparing: first the number before the decimal point, then the digits after the point place by place from the left. Fill missing places with zeros: $0.5 = 0.50 > 0.45$.

Rounding: as with natural numbers, the digit to the right of the rounding place decides. To tenths: $3.46 \approx 3.5$ · to hundredths: $2.718 \approx 2.72$

Longer is not bigger: 0.45 has more digits than 0.5 but is smaller. Five tenths are more than four tenths.

Rounded zeros stay: 4.996 rounded to hundredths is 5.00. The zeros show how precisely it was rounded.

INTERACTIVE · COMPARING DECIMALS
EXAMPLE 3 · ORDERING

Put in order: 0.7, 0.07, 0.707, 0.77, 0.077

Fill up to three places: 0.700, 0.070, 0.707, 0.770, 0.077.

0.07 < 0.077 < 0.7 < 0.707 < 0.77

EXAMPLE 4 · PER CENT

There are 20 pupils in 5c, and 7 of them play an instrument. What percentage is that?

$\tfrac{7}{20} = \tfrac{35}{100}$

35%

EXERCISES

Write as a percentage: a) $\tfrac{3}{10}$   b) $\tfrac{9}{100}$   c) 0.6   d) 0.05   e) $\tfrac{2}{5}$

a) 30%   b) 9%   c) 60%   d) 5%   e) 40%

Fill in $<$ or $>$: a) 0.8 ▢ 0.79   b) 3.05 ▢ 3.5   c) 12.1 ▢ 9.99   d) 0.099 ▢ 0.1

a) $>$   b) $<$   c) $>$   d) $<$

Round to tenths and to hundredths: a) 4.567   b) 0.349   c) 9.995

a) 4.6 and 4.57   b) 0.3 and 0.35   c) 10.0 and 10.00

In the 100 m race these times were measured in seconds: Ida 14.08 · Max 14.8 · Ole 14.18 · Pia 13.99. Who won? Give the order.

Less time is better: Pia (13.99), Ida (14.08), Ole (14.18), Max (14.8).

A battery shows 40% and holds 3,000 mAh (milliampere hours) when full. How much is still in it? What percentage is missing?

40% = $\tfrac{4}{10}$ of 3,000 mAh = 1,200 mAh. 60% is missing.

Find three decimals between 0.3 and 0.31. Is there a decimal that comes directly after 0.3?

For example 0.301, 0.305, 0.309. No: between two different decimals you can always find another one by adding a further place.

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Complete the table: fraction $\tfrac{1}{20}$, decimal 0.8, percentage 15%. Find the other two ways of writing each.

$\tfrac{1}{20} = 0.05 = 5\%$ · $\tfrac45 = 0.8 = 80\%$ · $\tfrac{3}{20} = 0.15 = 15\%$

Connecting with chapter 2.1: Which fraction is bigger, $\tfrac{5}{8}$ or $\tfrac{3}{5}$? Decide by writing both as decimals.

$\tfrac58 = 0.625$ and $\tfrac35 = 0.6$: $\tfrac58$ is bigger.

A jumper costs €40. In the sale there is a 25% discount. How much does it cost then?

25% is a quarter: €10 discount; the jumper costs €30.

A number with two decimal places was rounded to tenths and gave 7.4. Which numbers can it have been?

All numbers from 7.35 to 7.44.

EXCURSIONHISTORY

The art of tenths

For a long time merchants in Europe calculated with ordinary fractions, with ells, feet and inches, with guilders, groschen and pfennigs, and every unit had its own conversion. In 1585 the Flemish engineer Simon Stevin published a small booklet in Leiden with the title De Thiende, “The Tenth”. In it he explained how you can calculate with decimals just as easily as with whole numbers.

Stevin did not yet know the decimal point. After every digit he wrote a circled number that gave its place: with him, 3.47 looked something like this: 3⓪ 4① 7②. Only later mathematicians used a point or a comma as the separator. Stevin also demanded that measures, weights and coins be divided decimally. That took a good 200 years more: the metre and the kilogram only came after the French Revolution.

Source: S. Stevin: De Thiende. Christoffel Plantijn, Leiden 1585; in French as La Disme in the same year. MacTutor History of Mathematics, biography of Simon Stevin.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

PLACES AFTER THE DECIMAL POINT

tenths, hundredths, thousandths

$3.47 = 3 + \tfrac{4}{10} + \tfrac{7}{100}$

CONVERTING

expand to a decimal fraction, then write with a decimal point

$\tfrac34 = \tfrac{75}{100} = 0.75 = 75\%$

PER CENT

per cent means hundredths

$\tfrac{7}{20} = \tfrac{35}{100} = 35\%$

COMPARING

make the same number of places after the decimal point, compare from the left

$0.50 > 0.45$

ROUNDING

the digit to the right decides

$2.718 \approx 2.72$
